src/evaluation.c

This file converts resolver outcomes into counts and chooses policies on calibration data. It keeps dangerous acceptance separate from rejection.

Count one outcome and update its denominators

Section titled “Count one outcome and update its denominators”

A resolved label contributes either a correct exact/fuzzy match, a wrong target or a rejection. Unknown and ambiguous labels have separate unsafe-acceptance buckets. Formatting-only inputs are excluded from fuzzy recall. With default costs, one unsafe acceptance costs 100 and a rejected recoverable typo costs 1.

Download complete source
1/** @file2 * [PM-Me3cU7] Count what happened, including safe rejection and unsafe acceptance.3 * A rejected typo loses coverage. An accepted wrong name can change a setting.4 * These must stay separate even when a weighted cost combines them.5 */6#include <math.h>7#include <string.h>8#include "pm.h"910/** Does formatting alone resolve this target? Such inputs are not fuzzy recall. */11static int has_normalized_exact_match(const Registry *registry, const char *input) {12    char normalized[KEY_MAX + 1];13    size_t index;14    if (!normalize(input, normalized, sizeof normalized)) return 0;15    for (index = 0; index < registry->n; ++index) {16        if (!strcmp(normalized, registry->p[index].normalized)) return 1;17    }18    return 0;19}2021/** Add exactly one outcome bucket, plus denominator counts used for percentages. */22void metrics_add(Metrics *metrics, const TestCase *test, const Resolution *result, const Registry *registry) {23    int accepted = match_is_accepted(result->status);24    ++metrics->total;25    if (test->expected == EXPECT_INVALID) { ++metrics->invalid; return; }26    if (test->expected == EXPECT_RESOLVED) {27        ++metrics->eligible;28        if (!has_normalized_exact_match(registry, test->input)) ++metrics->fuzzy_inputs;29        if (accepted) {30            int wrong_target = strcmp(registry->p[result->first].name, test->target) != 0;31            if (wrong_target) ++metrics->wrong;32            else if (result->status == MATCH_EXACT) ++metrics->exact;33            else ++metrics->fuzzy;34        } else ++metrics->rejected;35    } else if (test->expected == EXPECT_UNKNOWN) {36        if (accepted) ++metrics->unknown_accept;37        else ++metrics->unknown_reject;38    } else if (accepted) ++metrics->ambiguous_accept;39    else if (result->status == MATCH_AMBIGUOUS) ++metrics->ambiguity;40    else ++metrics->ambiguous_unknown; /* Safe rejection, but the diagnosis missed ambiguity. */41}4243/** Default cost: one unsafe assignment costs as much as 100 rejected typos. */44double metric_cost(const Metrics *metrics, Costs costs) {45    unsigned dangerous_accepts = metrics->wrong + metrics->unknown_accept + metrics->ambiguous_accept;46    return costs.severe * (double)dangerous_accepts + costs.rejection * (double)metrics->rejected;47}48

Search policy settings using cached calibration scores

Section titled “Search policy settings using cached calibration scores”

Each calibration name is prepared and scored once. The nested grid changes thresholds, margins and optional edit caps without changing scores. Equal cost prefers a higher threshold, then a higher margin. Held-out cases do not enter this function. Calibration uses large static caches outside the timed resolution path.

49/** [PM-Ca8qD4] Calibration moves policy knobs, not algorithm scores.50 * Prepare/score once -> try each threshold/gap/cap -> count cost -> keep minimum.51 * The caller passes calibration data only. Held-out evaluation comes later.52 * Equal cost: prefer higher threshold, then higher margin; retain the first cap.53 */54Policy calibrate(const Dataset *dataset, size_t algorithm, Costs costs, double *chosen_cost, FILE *grid) {55    /* Static storage keeps this large cache off the call stack. Row c belongs56     * to case c; only that case's registry columns are read. Reuse is sequential,57     * so this calibration routine is not reentrant or thread-safe. */58    static double scores[MAX_CASES][MAX_PROPERTIES];59    static Prepared prepared[MAX_CASES];60    const double margins[] = {0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.20};61    const int edit_caps[] = {-1, 1, 2, 3};62    int is_edit_algorithm = algorithm >= 1 && algorithm <= 4;63    size_t threshold_count = algorithm ? 27U : 1U;64    size_t margin_count = algorithm ? 7U : 1U;65    size_t cap_count = is_edit_algorithm ? 4U : 1U;66    size_t case_index, threshold_index, margin_index, cap_index;67    double lowest_cost = 1e100;68    Policy winner = {1.000001, 0.20, -1};6970    for (case_index = 0; case_index < dataset->n; ++case_index) {71        const TestCase *test = &dataset->cases[case_index];72        Registry *registry = registry_get(test->schema);73        if (!prepare(test->input, &prepared[case_index])) continue;74        score_candidates(registry, &prepared[case_index], algorithm, scores[case_index]);75    }76    for (threshold_index = 0; threshold_index < threshold_count; ++threshold_index) {77        for (margin_index = 0; margin_index < margin_count; ++margin_index) {78            for (cap_index = 0; cap_index < cap_count; ++cap_index) {79                Policy policy = {threshold_index == 26 ? 1.000001 : 0.5 + 0.02 * (double)threshold_index,80                                 margins[margin_index], edit_caps[cap_index]};81                Metrics metrics = {0};82                double cost;83                int lower_cost, equal_cost, stricter_threshold, stricter_margin;84                for (case_index = 0; case_index < dataset->n; ++case_index) {85                    const TestCase *test = &dataset->cases[case_index];86                    Registry *registry = registry_get(test->schema);87                    Resolution result = decide(registry, &prepared[case_index], algorithm, policy, scores[case_index]);88                    metrics_add(&metrics, test, &result, registry);89                }90                cost = metric_cost(&metrics, costs);91                lower_cost = cost < lowest_cost - 1e-9;92                equal_cost = fabs(cost - lowest_cost) <= 1e-9;93                stricter_threshold = policy.threshold > winner.threshold;94                stricter_margin = policy.threshold == winner.threshold && policy.margin > winner.margin;95                if (lower_cost || (equal_cost && (stricter_threshold || stricter_margin))) {96                    lowest_cost = cost;97                    winner = policy;98                }99                if (grid) {100                    unsigned dangerous = metrics.wrong + metrics.unknown_accept + metrics.ambiguous_accept;101                    double coverage = metrics.eligible ? (double)(metrics.exact + metrics.fuzzy) / (double)metrics.eligible : 0;102                    fprintf(grid, "%s,%.6f,%.4f,%d,%u,%u,%u,%.6f,%.2f\n", algorithms[algorithm].id,103                            policy.threshold, policy.margin, policy.max_edits, metrics.fuzzy, dangerous,104                            metrics.rejected, coverage, cost);105                }106            }107        }108    }109    *chosen_cost = lowest_cost;110    return winner;111}112

Evaluate held-out labels once under the frozen policy

Section titled “Evaluate held-out labels once under the frozen policy”

Each result feeds both the overall metrics and one category. The saved record includes suggestions and the intended target index for later diagnostics. Rejecting an ambiguous label as unknown has zero dangerous-assignment cost, but still fails the stricter ambiguity-diagnosis label. This distinction remains visible in the report.

Reference for the contracts used in this file

Section titled “Reference for the contracts used in this file”

The project methodology defines outcome buckets, the separate calibration split and the safety cost model. These are experimental labels and policies, not mathematical properties of a distance. Open reference.

113/** A safe unknown response to an ambiguous label is a diagnostic failure, cost 0. */114static int expected_outcome_failed(const TestCase *test, const Resolution *result, int target_index) {115    int accepted = match_is_accepted(result->status);116    if (test->expected == EXPECT_RESOLVED) return !accepted || result->first != target_index;117    if (test->expected == EXPECT_UNKNOWN) return accepted;118    if (test->expected == EXPECT_AMBIGUOUS) return result->status != MATCH_AMBIGUOUS;119    return result->status != MATCH_INVALID;120}121122/** [PM-Ev6jH2] Use frozen policy once per held-out case; preserve every result.123 * One result feeds both the overall count and its category count, preventing drift.124 */125void evaluate(const Dataset *dataset, size_t algorithm, Policy policy, Evaluation *evaluation) {126    size_t case_index;127    memset(&evaluation->metrics, 0, sizeof evaluation->metrics);128    memset(evaluation->category, 0, sizeof evaluation->category);129    for (case_index = 0; case_index < dataset->n; ++case_index) {130        const TestCase *test = &dataset->cases[case_index];131        Registry *registry = registry_get(test->schema);132        Resolution result = resolve(registry, test->input, algorithm, policy);133        CaseResult *record = &evaluation->results[case_index];134        int category = category_index(test->category);135        size_t property_index;136        record->resolution = result;137        record->target = -1;138        for (property_index = 0; property_index < registry->n; ++property_index) {139            if (!strcmp(test->target, registry->p[property_index].name)) record->target = (int)property_index;140        }141        record->failure = expected_outcome_failed(test, &result, record->target);142        metrics_add(&evaluation->metrics, test, &result, registry);143        if (category >= 0) metrics_add(&evaluation->category[category], test, &result, registry);144    }145}
